name: rollapply
title: Apply a function to rolling windows

origin.description: Apply a function to each rolling window of a series.
origin.usage: rollapply(data, width, FUN, ..., by = 1, by.column = TRUE, fill = if (na.pad) NA, na.pad = FALSE, partial = FALSE, align = c("center", "left", "right"), coredata = TRUE)

arguments.name: data
arguments.text: Series, vector, or matrix.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: Window width, a vector of widths, or a list of offsets from the current time.

arguments.name: FUN
arguments.text: Function applied to each window.
Further arguments passed to FUN.

arguments.name: by
arguments.text: Step between windows when width has length 1.

arguments.name: by.column
arguments.text: Apply FUN to each column when TRUE.

arguments.name: fill
arguments.text: Three fill values for the left side, the interior gaps, and the right side. A shorter vector is recycled and a longer one keeps the first three. NULL drops those positions. "extend" repeats an end and linearly interpolates an interior gap.

arguments.name: na.pad
arguments.text: Deprecated. TRUE is fill = NA.

arguments.name: partial
arguments.text: FALSE needs every offset in range. TRUE passes the offsets that are in range. A number is the smallest count that is still evaluated. A negative number means a full window.

arguments.name: align
arguments.text: Where the window sits on its result time: center, left, or right. A unique prefix is enough. NULL selects center. Ignored when width is an offset list.

arguments.name: coredata
arguments.text: TRUE passes the window values. FALSE passes the series slice.

origin.details: A numeric width is turned into offsets by align. A list is already offsets. A length-1 width is placed at every by-th time, starting late enough that a full window fits unless partial allows a short one. Points outside the series are omitted when partial is false. fill follows na.fill: three components for the left, the interior, and the right. mean, max, and an odd median with no extra arguments use the faster rolling functions. An empty series is returned unchanged.
origin.value: A series of the same kind as data. Windows that were not computed are dropped when fill is omitted, or filled when fill is set.

translation.description: Apply a function to each rolling window of a series.
translation.usage: rollapply(data, width, FUN, *args, by=1, by_column=True, fill=None, na_pad=False, partial=False, align="center", coredata=True, **kwargs)

arguments.name: data
arguments.text: Series, vector, or matrix. A Zoo keeps its index.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: Window width, a vector of widths, or a list of offset vectors. None in that list skips the time.

arguments.name: FUN
arguments.text: Function applied to each window.

arguments.name: *args
arguments.text: Further positional arguments for FUN.

arguments.name: by
arguments.text: Step between windows when width has length 1. This is by in R.

arguments.name: by_column
arguments.text: Apply FUN to each column when True. This is by.column in R.

arguments.name: fill
arguments.text: Three fill values for the left side, the interior gaps, and the right side. A shorter vector is recycled and a longer one keeps the first three. NULL drops those positions. "extend" repeats an end and linearly interpolates an interior gap. Omitted means the short result, the same as a missing fill.

arguments.name: na_pad
arguments.text: Deprecated. True fills with NA. This is na.pad in R.

arguments.name: partial
arguments.text: False needs every offset in range. True passes the offsets that are in range. A number is the smallest count that is still evaluated. A negative number means a full window.

arguments.name: align
arguments.text: Where the window sits on its result time: center, left, or right. A unique prefix is enough. NULL selects center. Ignored when width is an offset list.

arguments.name: coredata
arguments.text: True passes the window values. False passes the Zoo slice.

arguments.name: **kwargs
arguments.text: Further named arguments for FUN.

translation.details: A numeric width is turned into offsets by align. A list is already offsets. A length-1 width is placed at every by-th time, starting late enough that a full window fits unless partial allows a short one. Points outside the series are omitted when partial is false. fill follows na.fill: three components for the left, the interior, and the right. mean, max, and an odd median with no extra arguments use the faster rolling functions. An empty series is returned unchanged.
translation.value: A series of the same kind as data. Windows that were not computed are dropped when fill is omitted, or filled when fill is set.
